iHeart Media | Audio Streaming Mobile App

Making digital audio more personal and interactive for the next generation of listeners

A redesigned listening experience that simplifies onboarding, personalizes discovery, and brings listeners closer through social interactions.

  • Consumer UX
  • Product Strategy
  • Interaction

Overview

iHeart Media struggled to retain listeners under 35. An 82% onboarding drop-off rate, navigational friction, and limited social connection pointed to an experience that felt demanding and impersonal. Our studio team combined interviews, review analysis, and heuristic evaluation to focus the redesign on navigation and community.

I facilitated the team’s work and pitched and owned Song Dedication. Together, we streamlined onboarding to get listeners to music faster and introduced Call Your Host and Song Dedication to bring the intimacy of live radio into the app. Usability findings also guided clearer location settings and playback feedback.

Key Impact

Increased content engagement by 18%

Online user testing with 45+ users showed higher content engagement and longer listening sessions. The redesign was developed for iHeart Media, whose wider audio network reaches 250M monthly listeners.

Product Designer & Product Manager

The Problem

Getting to the music took effort. Connection stopped at playback.

For a new listener, creating an account was only the beginning. The team found friction in onboarding and navigation, followed by an experience with few opportunities for personal connection. We needed to make listening easier to start and participation easier to understand.

How might we help younger listeners start listening with less effort and participate without losing the simplicity of audio?

Research Insights

Research pointed to clarity and connection.

5 interviews500+ reviewsHeuristic evaluation

We combined listener interviews with Reddit and App Store reviews and an evaluation of the existing experience. The synthesis brought three design implications into focus.

From documented evidence to design implications
EvidenceInsightDesign implication
Onboarding questions and flow created difficulty.The first session needed less effort.Clarify questions and remove unnecessary steps.
Navigation and controls were hard to understand.Useful features needed more visible entry points.Surface settings and explain actions.
Interview feedback expressed a desire for human interaction.Connection mattered alongside content.Explore dedications and episode-level participation.

Concept Evaluation

Explore widely. Focus on a more personal listening experience.

We explored six ways to help younger listeners get started, discover relevant content, and connect: onboarding and feature introductions, podcast live chat, curated radio playlists, Melody Match, hands-free mode, and live event participation.

Prototype Focus

We reviewed the concepts with our sponsors, weighing feasibility, potential impact, and fit with user and business needs. We narrowed the prototype to simpler onboarding, more personal discovery, and social features that bring listeners closer.

Onboarding
Remove unnecessary screens and make setup questions more relevant, so listeners can get to music faster.
Personalization
Bring liked and downloaded content into My Library, with access to genre and artist preferences.
Call Your Host
Give listeners a direct way to join an on-air discussion with the show’s host.
Live Chat
Connect listeners through conversations around the current radio program.
Song Dedication
Let listeners dedicate a song and send a personal message to someone special.

Testing & Iterations

Testing changed where controls lived—and what they said.

In usability sessions with 10+ users, we observed independent app exploration, including onboarding. We looked for confusion, frustration, and unmet expectations. Two findings led to more visible settings and clearer playback feedback.

Put location where listeners looked for it.

Initial approach
Location was nested under Advanced Settings.
Testing finding
Listeners expected it in account or profile settings.
Design change
Surface location selection directly in the profile.

Name the action instead of asking people to infer it.

Initial approach
An unlabeled plus action marked an episode played.
Testing finding
The meaning of the episode controls was unclear.
Design change
Add explicit Played feedback to the action row.

The Impact

A more engaging listening experience.

Online user testing with 45+ users showed an 18% increase in content engagement, contributing to longer listening sessions. Clearer onboarding and opportunities to participate helped make the experience more personal.

Observed changes
Location surfaced in profile; Played state made explicit.
Demonstrated scope
Onboarding, song dedication, and podcast participation.
Validation
Online user testing with 45+ users.

Reflections

What I’ll carry forward.

Leading a design team means creating alignment, not controlling every decision.

Working with a seven-person team taught me that effective product leadership is about creating alignment rather than directing every decision. Balancing different perspectives while maintaining a shared vision strengthened my ability to facilitate collaboration, communicate design rationale, and guide a team toward actionable outcomes.

Prioritization is about choosing what not to build.

Exploring concepts ranging from karaoke to live discussions and song dedication reinforced the importance of strategic prioritization. I learned to evaluate ideas against user needs, feasibility, and product goals rather than pursuing every interesting opportunity. This experience strengthened my ability to turn broad creative exploration into a focused product direction.
